purpose: The single authority for what a change invalidates. 'Product changed' is NEVER a reason to rerun everything. Each entry: change surface → micro-shards to rerun (+ optional short integration note).

change_rules.change: camera code (scan-capture camera path, camera permission handling, capture association)
print code (print dialogs, print buttons, print handlers)
CSV import code (import dialog, import API, template)
change_rules.integration: one short patient-count sanity check (dashboard counts) if the import API changed

change_rules.change: CSV export code (export button, export API, header schema)
backup code (backup trigger, ZIP builder, backup contents)
patient selection/delete code (Select Patients mode, delete selected, patient CRUD store)
change_rules.integration: one concise doctor workflow (EN) — patient family is the data spine

change_rules.change: page.tsx / app shell (navigation, view switching, scroll behavior)

change_rules.integration: the concise doctor workflow EN + AR + final security pass

change_rules.change: documents upload/viewer code (upload paths, document-viewer, zoom, annotations)
i18n touching UI (translation catalogs, RTL foundation, language switcher)
rerun: BROAD-parallel: every qa-*-ar micro-shard + qa-rtl-layout + qa-en-ui-spotcheck
then the representative AR doctor workflow
change_rules.integration: Arabic acceptance checklist (RTL direction, mirroring, long strings, wrapping, dialog overflow, button clipping, mixed text, dates/numbers, dark mode AR)

change_rules.change: Reset All Data removal / bulk patient management code
harness/CI-only (probe scripts, workflow yml, no product files in diff)
change_rules.integration: none — evidence stands; only the affected micro-shard's own rerun if its probe changed

notes: The registry (green-evidence.json) is the record; this map is the decision procedure.
When a fix worker touches multiple rules, union the rerun sets — but still in PARALLEL micro-shards, never a giant serial shard.
ENV records (physical camera, physical printer) never block and never expand a rerun set.
